Let’s talk about Chapter 12: Living with Uncertainty—Adapting to a Changing World.
Our world is shifting in ways no one can truly predict. Species are disappearing, ecosystems are transforming, and new challenges seem to pop up just when we think we’ve got things figured out. It’s no wonder so many of us feel anxious when we think about the future—there are no guarantees.
Imagine a family, packing up their home as the sea slowly creeps closer, not knowing what tomorrow will bring. Or a scientist, watching the skies as birds migrate, wondering which ones will make it and which might be lost for good. These aren’t rare stories anymore—they’re becoming the new normal, as people everywhere try to adjust to a world that’s constantly changing.
So, what does it really mean to live with uncertainty? It’s about accepting that we can’t control everything—and that’s okay. We need flexibility, a bit of resilience, and an open mind that’s ready to learn from mistakes. Some communities are already finding creative ways to adapt. They’re building homes that can take on floods, planting crops that thrive in new climates, and creating networks where people support one another through tough times.
What’s become clear is that adaptation isn’t just about getting by—it’s about finding meaning and purpose as things change. The sixth extinction reminds us that life never stands still; it’s always evolving. Our challenge is to keep moving forward, to stay humble, to learn from what’s come before, and to shape a future that really values the beauty and diversity of life on this planet.
